findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice mcqs for Chapter 2 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Computer Science Board shape (8 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 87 questions numbered 1-87; by section: 2.1 9, 2.2 10, 2.3 7, 2.4 10, 2.5 8, 2.6 6, 2.7 9, 2.8 8, 2.9 8, 2.10 6, 2.11 6. Keys: {'a': 22, 'b': 22, 'c': 22, 'd': 21}.

Covers every section in book order: computational thinking and its real-life examples, identifying a problem, decomposition, step-by-step solutions (algorithms), evaluating solutions, logic as knowledge representation, propositions, simple and compound propositions, AND/OR/NOT, truth values and 2^n rows, creating and using truth tables, equivalence, satisfiability, predicate logic, predicates and variables, propositional vs predicate logic, universal and existential quantifiers, relationships and library rules, inference and deduction. None repeats the chapter exercise. Every truth value and equivalence / satisfiability answer was computed in Python from the AND, OR and NOT definitions of the chapter.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
